'''Tryphon Thomas Georgiou''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|ɡ|iː|ɔːr|dʒ|uː}}, {{langx|el|Τρύφων Θωμάς Γεωργίου|}} {{IPA|el|ˈtrifon θoˈmas ʝeorˈʝiu|pron}}; born 18 October 1956) is a Greek and American [[electrical engineer]] and [[Applied mathematics|applied mathematician]]. He has made contributions to [[control theory]] and [[dynamical systems]]. Since 2016, he has been a distinguished professor of mechanical and aerospace engineering at the [[University of California, Irvine]] (UCI).

==Early life and education==
Georgiou was born in [[Athens]] in 1956. He earned a diploma in Mechanical and Electrical Engineering from the [[National Technical University of Athens]] in 1979 and a [[doctorate]] in electrical engineering from the [[University of Florida]] in 1983. He was advised by [[Rudolf E. Kálmán]] and wrote a dissertation on [[covariance]] sequences in [[stochastic control]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Georgiou |first1=Tryphon T. |title=To Rudolf E. Kalman: A personal Goodbye |journal=IEEE Control Systems |date=17 March 2017 |url=https://georgiou.eng.uci.edu/publications/personal.pdf |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>

==Career==

After completing his doctorate, Georgiou joined the faculty of [[Florida Atlantic University]] in 1983 and [[Iowa State University]] in 1986. He joined the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1989, where he was professor for nearly three decades and director of the Control Science and Dynamical Systems Center beginning in 1990.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=Biography: Tryphon T. Georgiou |url=https://georgiou.eng.uci.edu/bio.html |website=georgiou.eng.uci.edu |publisher=UC Irvine Engineering |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref> He also served as Vincentine Hermes-Luh Chair in Electrical and Computer Engineering from 2002 to 2016.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tryphon Georgiou |url=https://cse.umn.edu/ece/tryphon-georgiou |website=cse.umn.edu |publisher=University of Minnesota: Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering |access-date=11 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

His research specializes in control theory, with an emphasis on stochastic and [[robust control]]. He made contributions to the development of the [[gap metric]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Georgiou |first1=Tryphon T. |title=On the computation of the gap metric |journal=Systems & Control Letters |date=1 October 1988 |volume=11 |issue=4 |pages=253–257 |doi=10.1016/0167-6911(88)90067-9 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/0167691188900679 |access-date=11 February 2026 |issn=0167-6911|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Georgiou |first1=T.T. |last2=Smith |first2=M.C. |chapter=Optimal robustness in the gap metric |title=Proceedings of the 28th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control |date=December 1989 |pages=2331–2336 vol.3 |doi=10.1109/CDC.1989.70590 }}</ref> for measuring distances between [[Dynamical system|dynamical systems]] and analyzing feedback robustness, including extensions to nonlinear systems. In 1997, he developed the [[Small-gain theorem|large-gain theorem]], providing quantitative conditions for stability in both linear and nonlinear settings, and worked on the [[separation principle in stochastic control]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chen |first1=Yongxin |last2=Georgiou |first2=Tryphon T. |last3=Pavon |first3=Michele |title=On the Relation Between Optimal Transport and Schrödinger Bridges: A Stochastic Control Viewpoint |journal=Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications |date=1 May 2016 |volume=169 |issue=2 |pages=671–691 |doi=10.1007/s10957-015-0803-z |url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10957-015-0803-z |access-date=11 February 2026|hdl=11577/3216967 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Francis |first1=Bruce A. |last2=Georgiou |first2=Tryphon T. |title=Stability theory for linear time-invariant plants with periodic digital controllers |journal=IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control |date=30 September 1988 |volume=33 |issue=9 |pages=820–832 |doi=10.1109/9.1310 |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/1310 |access-date=11 February 2026|url-access=subscription }}</ref> Along with [[Malcolm C. Smith]], [[Christopher I. Byrnes]], and [[Anders Lindquist]], Georgiou also works on stochastic control problems, including state [[Structural equation modeling|covariance steering]] and [[Linear–quadratic–Gaussian control|Linear-quadratic-Gaussian control]]. He has also made contributions to network models for disease spread in [[epidemiology]],<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Taghvaei |first1=Amirhossein |last2=Georgiou |first2=Tryphon T. |last3=Norton |first3=Larry |last4=Tannenbaum |first4=Allen |title=Fractional SIR epidemiological models |journal=Scientific Reports |date=30 November 2020 |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=20882 |doi=10.1038/s41598-020-77849-7  |doi-access=free|pmid=33257790 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-020-77849-7 |access-date=11 February 2026 |language=en |issn=2045-2322|pmc=7705759 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Khong |first1=Sei Zhen |last2=Su |first2=Lanlan |last3=Georgiou |first3=Tryphon |title=Long-term susceptible fractions in networked epidemic models and their relation to the basic reproduction number |journal=Scientific Reports |date=3 November 2025 |volume=15 |issue=1 |pages=38429 |doi=10.1038/s41598-025-22158-0  |doi-access=free|pmid=41184313 |pmc=12583584 |language=en |issn=2045-2322}}</ref> market fragility in financial systems,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Sandhu |first1=Romeil S. |last2=Georgiou |first2=Tryphon T. |last3=Tannenbaum |first3=Allen R. |title=Ricci curvature: An economic indicator for market fragility and systemic risk |journal=Science Advances |date=27 May 2016 |volume=2 |issue=5 |article-number=e1501495 |doi=10.1126/sciadv.1501495 |pmid=27386522 |url=https://www.science.org/doi/full/10.1126/sciadv.1501495 |access-date=11 February 2026 |language=en}}</ref> and neural connectivity in the brain.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Farooq |first1=Hamza |last2=Chen |first2=Yongxin |last3=Georgiou |first3=Tryphon T. |last4=Tannenbaum |first4=Allen |last5=Lenglet |first5=Christophe |title=Network curvature as a hallmark of brain structural connectivity |journal=Nature Communications |date=30 October 2019 |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=4937 |doi=10.1038/s41467-019-12915-x  |doi-access=free|pmid=31666510 |pmc=6821808 |language=en |issn=2041-1723}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Fuster |first1=Andrea |last2=Ghosh |first2=Aurobrata |last3=Kaden |first3=Enrico |last4=Rathi |first4=Yogesh |last5=Reisert |first5=Marco |title=Computational Diffusion MRI: MICCAI Workshop, Munich, Germany, October 9th, 2015 |date=8 April 2016 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-319-28588-7 |page=55 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iNr7CwAAQBAJ&dq=tryphon+georgiou&pg=PA55 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2016, he became a distinguished professor at the [[UC Irvine Samueli School of Engineering|Samueli School of Engineering]] at UC Irvine.<ref name=":0" /> He has been on the board of governors for the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers|IEEE]] since 2002.<ref name=":0" /> He is a fellow of the [[International Federation of Automatic Control]] (IFAC) since 2016 and the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) since 2021.<ref name=":0" />
